useCase.name: Rank students into an ordered merit list and control how much of it families are shown

intent.name: merit.list.generate
intent.summary: Rank the students in scope into an ordered list on a stated criterion. One step, and nobody sees it yet.

request.text: kisi bache ki position theek kar do

routesElsewhere.note: The list reads approved results and never changes them. Correcting a position means correcting a mark and regenerating (BR-11).

steps.note: One step. Every subject result for the exam must be approved first (BR-1) — a ranking built on part of the marks is not a ranking.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. An unapproved subject result blocks the list outright; students with unresolved absences and mixed subject sets are handled within the run and reported.
plan.atomicity: One write: the list, its positions, its exclusions and the criterion used together or not at all (BR-9). Nothing is visible to any family — the Principal or School Admin approves it and the Coordinator then chooses what is published, because a ranking published wrongly cannot be unseen (BR-4).

parameters.name: criterion

fields.name: excluded_students

errors.meaning: A subject result for the exam is not yet approved.

errors.meaning: Every student in scope has an unresolved absence.
The scope holds students who took different subject sets.
errors.written: Separate lists, one per subject set.
errors.note: Not a refusal. Ranking by total marks compares only students who sat the same subjects (BR-8) — report that more than one list came out.

planningRules.rule: Never choose the ranking criterion. Total marks, percentage and weighted score produce different orders (BR-9), and a planner that picked one has decided who comes first.
Never approve a subject result to make a list possible. E1 is BR-1 working, and releasing a result puts a grade in front of every family as a side effect of wanting a ranking.

Report the excluded students and why. A student with an unresolved absence is left out until the makeup is marked or the absence is finalised (BR-2), and their family will not find them on a list nobody explained.
Report shared positions plainly. Equal marks share a position and the next is skipped — two students placed second are followed by a fourth, not a third (BR-3).
Report where more than one list came out. In a Subject Wise class students take different subjects, and one list across them would compare figures that are not comparable (BR-8, E3).
Never describe the list as published. Nothing is visible to any family until it is approved and a publication choice is made (BR-4, BR-5).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A list is regenerated rather than withdrawn while unpublished. Once published, withdrawal carries a reason (BR-7).

steps.note: One step, and it reaches every family in scope. The choice decides what each of them learns (BR-5, BR-6).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Publication before approval, and publication with no choice made, are both refused.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the publication and the messages to families together or not at all. Each family is told their own child's position; where the school chose to announce them, the first, second and third are told to all (BR-5). A family never sees another child's position beyond that (BR-6). It cannot be unseen — a wrong list is withdrawn with a reason, but the households that read it have read it (BR-4, BR-7).

planningRules.rule: Never default the publication choice. Whether the school names its top three to every household is a decision about the school (BR-5, E6), and a planner that chose has made it.
Never publish more of the list than the choice allows. A family never sees another child's position beyond the top three where the school chose to announce them (BR-6).
Never publish an out-of-date list. A mark has changed and the order may have changed with it (E8) — regenerating costs nothing, and an unseen wrong ranking cannot be unsent.
Report the excluded students. Their families are told no position at all (BR-2), and on a day the top three are announced that absence is conspicuous.
Never read positions out to anybody who is not entitled to them. The same rule that governs publication governs the reply.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the reason. A published ranking being taken down is something families will ask about, and the answer is the school's.
Never describe withdrawal as undoing the publication. Families who were told a position still hold it (BR-4) — the correction reaches them only when a recalculated list is reissued (BR-7).
Report how many families were already told. That is the size of what has to be put right, and it is invisible from the word withdrawn.
Never chain a regeneration onto the withdrawal. The mark has to be corrected first, and the list built again reads the corrected results (BR-11).
